high.title: Deputy Prime Minister Demands Interest Rate Cuts to Lowest Possible Level
high.summary: At the government's regular meeting on May 4, Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang acknowledged the State Bank of Vietnam's efforts in monetary policy management, particularly directing banks to reduce lending rates. However, he demanded more effective and substantial solutions, emphasizing that "we must ensure lending rates are at the lowest possible level" while prioritizing credit for production and business sectors. This signals potential further monetary easing ahead, which could weaken VND and support government bond demand if rates fall further. FX and bond traders should monitor for specific rate guidance from SBV and any formal policy rate cuts in coming weeks.

high.title: Agribank Gets Moody's Rating Outlook Upgraded from "Stable" to "Positive"
high.summary: Moody's Ratings upgraded Agribank's rating outlook from "Stable" to "Positive," reflecting improved assessment of Vietnam's macroeconomic environment and sovereign creditworthiness. This follows Moody's upgrade of Vietnam's sovereign outlook to "Positive" on May 4, 2026. Moody's praised Vietnam's improving economic competitiveness through digitalization, infrastructure investment, and capital market development. For Agribank, they highlighted stable funding base with large diverse customer base and steady asset quality. The upgrade signals potential sovereign rating improvement ahead, which would be positive for VND and Vietnamese government bonds. International fund managers should watch for sovereign rating action that could lift the entire Vietnamese credit curve.

medium.title: Fifth Largest Bank Sees Asset Decline as Customers Withdraw Over 15,000 Billion VND in Deposits
medium.summary: MB Bank reported Q1 2026 total assets of 1,611 trillion VND, down 4,500 billion VND (0.3%) from year-end 2025, though still up 39% year-over-year. The decline was mainly due to reduced deposits at the State Bank of Vietnam, falling from 68,494 billion VND to 15,156 billion VND. This reflects banking system liquidity dynamics and potential monetary policy impacts on deposit flows.

medium.title: VN-Index Breaks 1,900 Points Milestone - Key Contributors Identified
medium.summary: VN-Index reached a new record high of 1,909.01 points on May 7, up 0.94%, surpassing the previous record of 1,902 points from January 13, 2026. Trading volume on HOSE exceeded 30,000 billion VND, up 15% from the previous session. Vingroup subsidiaries VHM (up ceiling) and VIC (up 2%) were the main drivers. This signals renewed confidence in Vietnamese equities despite ongoing global uncertainties.

medium.title: Securities Sector Capital Increase Wave - First Company to Exceed 30,000 Billion VND
medium.summary: S&I Ratings reports 2026 as a dynamic period for capital increases in the securities sector, driven by three factors: 100% foreign room opening, margin lending limits approaching, and higher risk coefficients. SSI plans to increase capital by 9,262 billion VND, potentially reaching over 30,000 billion VND charter capital by year-end, making it the first securities company to reach this scale.

medium.title: VN-Index Could Reach 2,300 Points According to Dragon Capital
medium.summary: Dragon Securities (VDSC) believes the market hasn't fully repriced strong Q1 2026 earnings. They see potential for further gains as geopolitical tensions may ease, though high risk premiums persist. The firm suggests markets are not lacking profit growth but confidence in earnings sustainability, indicating room for valuation expansion if Middle East tensions cool.
